html:
Nobatia was a kingdom in Lower Nubia, along the Nile in what is now southern Egypt and northern Sudan, from about 400 until it merged with Makuria around 700. It is shown here in 600 and 700. It was one of three Nubian kingdoms that followed the fall of Kush, with Makuria and Alodia to the south.

The Nobatians pushed the Blemmyes out of the Nile valley and ruled from Faras. Their kings were buried with rich goods at Ballana and Qustul. In the 540s missionaries sent with the backing of Empress Theodora won the court over, and Nobatia converted to Christianity.

Its southern neighbour, Makuria, fought off the Arab armies from Egypt in 652 and agreed the baqt, a treaty of trade and tribute that lasted for centuries. At some point in the 7th or early 8th century Nobatia was joined to Makuria, and the united kingdom kept the name Makuria. Faras cathedral, with its wall paintings, was a centre of Nubian Christianity.
